question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Consicstent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Consicstent" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "consistent", meaning acting or behaving in the same way over time; unchanging, steady. (सुसंगत / एकरूप)

◦ Example: She has been a consistent performer throughout the season.

• Spelling key: CON + SIS + TENT (no extra "c" in the middle).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Trifle" (a thing of little value/importance), "Surrender" (to give up) and "Disgust" (a strong feeling of dislike) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related forms: consistent (adjective), consistency (noun), consistently (adverb). Antonym: inconsistent. Such "one wrong letter inserted" spellings are common SSC traps — read each option letter by letter.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Ecstatic
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Happy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ecstatic" means feeling or expressing overwhelming happiness or joyful excitement. Its closest synonym among the options is "happy". (अत्यंत आनंदित / परम प्रसन्न)

◦ Example: The fans were ecstatic when India won the World Cup.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Shocked" (surprised/upset), Option 3 "Angry" (feeling anger) and Option 4 "Interested" (showing curiosity) do not convey the sense of great joy.

NOTE

• Synonyms of ecstatic: elated, overjoyed, euphoric, thrilled, rapturous, on cloud nine. Antonyms: miserable, depressed, dejected. The noun form is "ecstasy" (परमानंद).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a phrasal verb error.

Mrs. Premlatha asked / Malini to hand down / all the / payment slips.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Malini to hand down.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "hand down" means to pass something (property, traditions, clothes) to a younger generation — it does not fit here. The correct phrasal verb is "hand over", meaning to give/submit something to someone.

◦ Correct: Mrs. Premlatha asked Malini to hand over all the payment slips.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Mrs. Premlatha asked", "all the" and "payment slips" are grammatically correct segments.

• "Hand down" example: This necklace was handed down from my grandmother.

NOTE

• Important "hand" phrasal verbs: hand over (give/submit — सौंपना), hand down (pass to the next generation), hand in (submit to an authority), hand out (distribute — बाँटना).

question: What does it imply when people say to ‘read between the lines’?
option_2: To read with an ability to infer the meaning
option_3: To skip initial and final lines in a paragraph
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To read with an ability to infer the meaning.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "read between the lines" means to understand the hidden or implied meaning of something that is not directly stated, i.e., to infer the real meaning. (छिपा हुआ अर्थ समझना)

◦ Example: If you read between the lines, his letter is actually a complaint.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (reading fast), Option 3 (skipping lines) and Option 4 (avoiding details) describe literal reading habits, not the idiomatic meaning of inferring what is unsaid.

NOTE

• Related idioms: "get the message" (understand the implied point), "take the hint" (understand an indirect suggestion). Idiom-based questions are frequent in SSC CGL/CHSL/MTS — always learn the figurative, not the literal, meaning.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The workers had been repairing / the mall road in / town for / several days now.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The workers had been repairing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The time expression "for several days now" (the word "now" connects the action to the present) requires the present perfect continuous tense — "have been repairing" — not the past perfect continuous "had been repairing".

◦ Correct: The workers have been repairing the mall road in town for several days now.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "the mall road in", "town for" and "several days now" are correct segments.

• "Had been + V-ing" (past perfect continuous) is used for an action continuing up to another past action, e.g., "They had been repairing the road for days when the floods came."

NOTE

• Present perfect continuous = has/have been + V-ing, used with "for + period" and "since + point of time" when the action continues till now. The word "now" in the sentence is the decisive clue.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A piece of cake
option_1: A slice of cake for eating
option_3: A cake which is sold as a piece
option_4: A cake that broke into pieces
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Easy to do or achieve.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a piece of cake" means something very easy to do or achieve. (बहुत आसान काम)

◦ Example: The maths paper was a piece of cake for Ravi — he finished it in half the time.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 3 and 4 give the literal meaning of cake pieces, which is not how idioms work — idioms carry a figurative meaning.

NOTE

• Similar idioms for "very easy": "a cakewalk", "child's play", "a walk in the park", "as easy as pie". Opposite idea: "a hard/tough nut to crack" (a difficult problem or person).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Cultural heritage is the lifeblood of any ________ and serves as a link between generations.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. civilisation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Civilisation" means an organised human society with its own culture and way of life. Cultural heritage is naturally the lifeblood of a civilisation and links its generations. (सभ्यता)

◦ Correct: Cultural heritage is the lifeblood of any civilisation and serves as a link between generations.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "lethargy" (laziness/lack of energy — सुस्ती) and Option 2 "birthright" (a right one has from birth) do not fit the sense.

• Option 4 "believe" is a verb; the blank needs a noun (the noun form is "belief").

NOTE

• "Civilisation" (British spelling) / "civilization" (American). Collocation: "ancient civilisation", "cradle of civilisation". "Lifeblood" = the most essential thing that keeps something alive and strong.

question:
Select the most appropriate verb form to fill in the blank.

Arun __________ his bicycle to school every day.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. rides.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The time expression "every day" indicates a habitual action, which takes the simple present tense. With the third person singular subject "Arun", the verb takes "-s" — "rides".

◦ Correct: Arun rides his bicycle to school every day.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "ride" lacks the required "-s" for a singular subject.

• Option 2 "riding" needs a helping verb (is riding) and would show a continuous action, not a habit.

• Option 4 "rode" is the past tense and clashes with "every day".

NOTE

• Simple present for habits/routines/universal truths: markers are every day, always, usually, often, daily. Rule: He/She/It/singular noun + V1 + s/es. Verb forms: ride – rode – ridden.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word 'pursue' from the given sentence.

Dr. Kalam's success in the field of science has inspired young Indians to dream big and chase those dreams with immense hard work.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. chase.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Pursue" means to follow or chase something in order to catch or achieve it (e.g., to pursue a goal/dream). In the sentence, the word "chase" (to run after, to strive for) is its synonym. (पीछा करना / लक्ष्य का अनुसरण करना)

◦ Example: She decided to pursue/chase her dream of becoming a doctor.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "inspired" (motivated), "immense" (huge) and "success" (achievement) do not mean "pursue".

NOTE

• Synonyms of pursue: chase, follow, seek, strive for, go after. Collocations: pursue a career/goal/dream/case. Antonyms: abandon, give up, shun.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

My secretary is disposed of / discuss everything in great detail / before she begins / the actual work.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. My secretary is disposed of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct expression is "be disposed to + verb", meaning to be inclined or willing to do something. "Dispose of" means to get rid of/throw away, which is wrong here. So it should be "My secretary is disposed to discuss ...".

◦ Correct: My secretary is disposed to discuss everything in great detail before she begins the actual work.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "discuss everything in great detail", "before she begins" and "the actual work" are correct segments.

• "Dispose of" example: Please dispose of the garbage properly.

NOTE

• Preposition pairs to remember: disposed to (inclined to — इच्छुक), dispose of (get rid of — निपटाना). Fixed preposition combinations are a favourite SSC error-spotting area (e.g., "abide by", "consist of", "prefer ... to").

question:
Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error.

The accideent on the highway caused a long traffic jam.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. accident.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "accident", meaning an unfortunate incident that happens unexpectedly, typically causing damage or injury. (दुर्घटना)

◦ Correct: The accident on the highway caused a long traffic jam.

• Spelling key: AC + CI + DENT (double "c", single "e" before "nt").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "accidnt" (missing "e"), Option 2 "acicdent" (letters jumbled) and Option 4 "acident" (single "c") are all misspelt.

NOTE

• Related forms: accidental (adjective), accidentally (adverb). Similar double-letter words often tested: occasion, accommodate, occurrence, recommend.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. One of them contains an error. Select the segment that contains the error from the given options.

Neither Smith / nor Rose / were in / the classroom.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. were in.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• With "neither ... nor", the verb agrees with the subject nearer to it. Here the nearer subject "Rose" is singular, so the verb must be "was", not "were".

◦ Correct: Neither Smith nor Rose was in the classroom.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Neither Smith", "nor Rose" and "the classroom" are correct segments.

• If the nearer subject were plural, the verb would be plural: "Neither the teacher nor the students were present."

NOTE

• Rule of proximity applies to: either ... or, neither ... nor, not only ... but also, or, nor — the verb agrees with the nearest subject. This subject–verb agreement rule is repeatedly asked in SSC CGL/CHSL/MTS.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word

The project’s tight deadline and complex requirements made it a gruelling task for the team.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Challenging.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gruelling" means extremely tiring, difficult and demanding great effort. Its closest synonym is "challenging". (अत्यंत थका देने वाला / कठिन)

◦ Example: The soldiers went through a gruelling/challenging training schedule.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Empowering" (giving power/confidence), Option 2 "Inclusive" (including everyone) and Option 4 "Accessible" (easy to reach or use) do not convey difficulty.

NOTE

• Synonyms of gruelling: exhausting, arduous, strenuous, taxing, punishing, laborious. Antonyms: easy, effortless, light. Spelling: "gruelling" (British) / "grueling" (American).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

He is _________ tired to finish his homework.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. too.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "too + adjective + to + verb" means so ... that one cannot — "He is too tired to finish his homework" = he is so tired that he cannot finish it. (इतना ... कि नहीं)

◦ Correct: He is too tired to finish his homework.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "to" is a preposition/infinitive marker, not a degree adverb.

• Options 3 "most" and 4 "more" are for comparison and do not fit "tired ... to finish".

NOTE

• "Too ... to" always carries a negative sense (too weak to walk). Compare: "He is so tired that he cannot finish his homework" and "He is very tired" (very = simply a high degree, no negative result).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Please listen to all announcements _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. attentively.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Attentively" means with full attention and concentration. One should listen to announcements attentively. (ध्यानपूर्वक)

◦ Correct: Please listen to all announcements attentively.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "easily" (without difficulty), Option 2 "generally" (usually) and Option 3 "hungrily" (with hunger/greed) do not collocate with "listen to announcements".

NOTE

• "Listen attentively/carefully" is a standard collocation. Adverb formation: adjective + "-ly" (attentive → attentively). Related words: attention (noun), attentive (adjective), attentiveness (noun).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Energy
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Power.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Energy" means the strength, vigour and capacity to do work or be active. Its closest synonym is "power". (ऊर्जा / शक्ति)

◦ Example: Young children are full of energy/power and enthusiasm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Frailty" (weakness — दुर्बलता) is an antonym of energy.

• Option 2 "strife" (conflict/quarrel) and Option 3 "Speed" (rate of motion) are not synonyms of energy.

NOTE

• Synonyms of energy: power, vigour, vitality, stamina, dynamism, strength. Antonyms: weakness, frailty, lethargy, exhaustion.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The detective's job was to discern the truth from the web of lies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Perceive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Discern" means to recognise, distinguish or perceive something clearly, especially with difficulty. Its closest synonym is "perceive". (पहचानना / समझना)

◦ Example: A good judge can discern/perceive the truth behind conflicting statements.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Ignore" (to take no notice of) is nearly opposite in sense.

• Option 2 "Confuse" (to mix up) and Option 4 "Fabricate" (to invent falsely, to make up) do not fit — in fact, "fabricate" relates to creating the "web of lies", not detecting the truth.

NOTE

• Synonyms of discern: perceive, detect, distinguish, recognise, make out. Related words: discernment (good judgement), discernible (noticeable).

question: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
option_2: The sun rises in the east.
option_3: We watches movies every Friday night.
option_4: He works as a software developer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. We watches movies every Friday night.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The plural subject "We" must take the base form of the verb (V1) in the simple present — "watch", not "watches". The "-es" form is only for third person singular (he/she/it).

◦ Correct: We watch movies every Friday night.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "She always eats" (she + eats ✔), Option 2 "The sun rises" (the sun + rises ✔ — universal truth) and Option 4 "He works" (he + works ✔) all show correct subject–verb agreement.

NOTE

• Simple present agreement: I/We/You/They + V1 (watch, eat, go); He/She/It + V1 + s/es (watches, eats, goes). Subject–verb agreement is among the most tested grammar rules in SSC exams.

question:
Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error.

The rainbow only appears after a hurican.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. hurricane.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "hurricane", meaning a violent tropical storm with very strong winds. (प्रचंड चक्रवाती तूफ़ान)

◦ Correct: The rainbow only appears after a hurricane.

• Spelling key: HUR + RI + CANE (double "r", ends in "-cane").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "hurrecane", "hurrecain" and "hurrican" are all misspelt forms.

NOTE

• GK link: the same storm system is called a hurricane in the Atlantic/Caribbean, a typhoon in the western Pacific (China/Japan) and a cyclone in the Indian Ocean region.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Accepting how wonderful you truly are and incorporating this _______ into your attitude and personality is perhaps one of the most difficult things to do in life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. insight.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Insight" means a deep and clear understanding of something. Realising "how wonderful you truly are" is an insight (an understanding about yourself) that can be incorporated into one's attitude and personality. (अंतर्दृष्टि / गहरी समझ)

◦ Correct: ... incorporating this insight into your attitude and personality ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "craziness" (madness), Option 3 "folly" (foolishness — मूर्खता) and Option 4 "glitch" (a small fault or malfunction) all carry negative senses that contradict "how wonderful you truly are".

NOTE

• Synonyms of insight: understanding, perception, awareness, discernment, intuition. Collocations: "gain insight into", "valuable insight", "deep insight".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

My next pet, Ari, was a pigeon. He became convinced that he was not a bird at all and refused to ____ 1 ___. If he wanted to get on a table or a chair, he stood below it, cooing until someone picked him up. He would even try to come ____ 2____ walks with us. This, however, we had to stop for, _____ 3____ you carried him on your shoulder or else you let him walk behind. If you let him walk, you had to slow down your own ______ 4_____ to suit his, for should you get too far ahead, you would find him running after you, cooing frantically, his chest pouted out with ______5_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. fly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ari was a pigeon (a bird) who "became convinced that he was not a bird at all", so the natural bird activity he refused to do was to "fly". (उड़ना)

◦ Correct: He became convinced that he was not a bird at all and refused to fly.

• The next lines confirm this — he waited to be picked up to get on a table or chair and walked behind people instead of flying.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "read" is absurd for a pigeon; Option 3 "flea" (a small jumping insect — noun) and Option 4 "file" (to arrange papers) make no sense.

• "Flea" is a homophone-like trap for "flee" (to run away) — note the difference: flea (insect), flee (escape).

NOTE

• In cloze passages, always read the sentences before and after the blank; here the contrast "not a bird at all" directly points to the bird's defining action — flying.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

My next pet, Ari, was a pigeon. He became convinced that he was not a bird at all and refused to ____ 1 ___. If he wanted to get on a table or a chair, he stood below it, cooing until someone picked him up. He would even try to come ____ 2____ walks with us. This, however, we had to stop for, _____ 3____ you carried him on your shoulder or else you let him walk behind. If you let him walk, you had to slow down your own ______ 4_____ to suit his, for should you get too far ahead, you would find him running after you, cooing frantically, his chest pouted out with ______5_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. on.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct preposition with "walks" is "on" — "to come on walks with us" (to accompany someone on a walk). (सैर पर साथ चलना)

◦ Correct: He would even try to come on walks with us.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "by walks", "at walks" and "in walks" are unidiomatic; English says "go/come on a walk", just as we say "on a trip", "on a journey", "on a picnic", "on a tour".

NOTE

• Preposition "on" with outings: on a walk, on a trip, on a tour, on an excursion, on holiday. Fixed preposition collocations are frequently tested in SSC cloze tests.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

My next pet, Ari, was a pigeon. He became convinced that he was not a bird at all and refused to ____ 1 ___. If he wanted to get on a table or a chair, he stood below it, cooing until someone picked him up. He would even try to come ____ 2____ walks with us. This, however, we had to stop for, _____ 3____ you carried him on your shoulder or else you let him walk behind. If you let him walk, you had to slow down your own ______ 4_____ to suit his, for should you get too far ahead, you would find him running after you, cooing frantically, his chest pouted out with ______5_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. either.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence offers two alternatives joined by "or else": "you carried him on your shoulder or else you let him walk behind". The correlative that pairs with "or/or else" is "either".

◦ Correct: ... for, either you carried him on your shoulder or else you let him walk behind.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "neither" pairs with "nor", not with "or else".

• Options 3 "never" and 4 "ever" are adverbs of time and cannot introduce the pair of alternatives.

NOTE

• Correlative conjunctions (used in pairs): either ... or, neither ... nor, both ... and, not only ... but also, whether ... or. The two joined parts must be grammatically parallel.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

My next pet, Ari, was a pigeon. He became convinced that he was not a bird at all and refused to ____ 1 ___. If he wanted to get on a table or a chair, he stood below it, cooing until someone picked him up. He would even try to come ____ 2____ walks with us. This, however, we had to stop for, _____ 3____ you carried him on your shoulder or else you let him walk behind. If you let him walk, you had to slow down your own ______ 4_____ to suit his, for should you get too far ahead, you would find him running after you, cooing frantically, his chest pouted out with ______5_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. pace.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Pace" means the speed of walking or moving. To let the slow-walking pigeon keep up, one had to "slow down your own pace to suit his". (चाल / गति)

◦ Correct: If you let him walk, you had to slow down your own pace to suit his ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "piece" (a part of something) and Option 2 "peace" (calm; absence of war) are homophone traps — they sound similar but have entirely different meanings.

• Option 4 "space" (empty area) does not fit "slow down".

NOTE

• Confusing word set: pace (speed of movement), peace (शांति), piece (टुकड़ा). Collocations with pace: "keep pace with", "at a snail's pace", "set the pace".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

My next pet, Ari, was a pigeon. He became convinced that he was not a bird at all and refused to ____ 1 ___. If he wanted to get on a table or a chair, he stood below it, cooing until someone picked him up. He would even try to come ____ 2____ walks with us. This, however, we had to stop for, _____ 3____ you carried him on your shoulder or else you let him walk behind. If you let him walk, you had to slow down your own ______ 4_____ to suit his, for should you get too far ahead, you would find him running after you, cooing frantically, his chest pouted out with ______5_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. indignation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Indignation" means anger or annoyance at being treated unfairly. The pigeon, left behind, ran after the walkers "cooing frantically, his chest pouted out with indignation" — i.e., puffed up in angry protest. (अपमानजनक व्यवहार पर क्रोध / रोष)

◦ Correct: ... his chest pouted out with indignation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "intimation" (a hint or announcement — सूचना), Option 3 "inclination" (a tendency or liking — झुकाव) and Option 4 "ignition" (the act of setting on fire; a car's starting mechanism) do not fit the bird's angry reaction.

NOTE

• Word family: indignant (adjective — feeling wronged), indignation (noun), indignantly (adverb). These four options are a classic similar-sounding words trap; always match the meaning to the context, not the sound.
